'''Ester Samuel-Cahn''' ({{Langx|he|אסתר שמואל-כחן}}; May 16, 1933 – November 20, 2015) was an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[statistician]] and educator. She was a [[Emeritus|professor emeritus]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title = Ester Samuel-Cahn|url = http://www.huji.ac.il/dataj/controller/ihoker/MOP-STAFF_LINK?sno=204678&Save_t=|website = The Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Faculty Research Interests|access-date = 2015-08-02}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Samuel-Cahn was born in [[Oslo]], Norway. During the [[German occupation of Norway|Nazi occupation of Norway]], in 1942, her father, a [[rabbi]], was warned that he would be arrested by the [[Nazi Germany|Germans]].<ref name=":0">{{cite magazine|title=Torchlighters 2008|location=Jerusalem|magazine=Yad Vashem Magazine|volume=49|date=April 2008|issn=0793-7199|page=12|url=https://www.yadvashem.org/sites/default/files/yv_magazine49.pdf|access-date=15 July 2018}}</ref> He refused to leave in order to try to support his community.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url = https://www.haaretz.com/news/features/this-day-in-jewish-history/1.631974|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141216121400/http://www.haaretz.com/news/features/this-day-in-jewish-history/1.631974|url-status = dead|archive-date = December 16, 2014|title = This Day in Jewish History / Norway chief rabbi who stayed with his flock dies in Auschwitz|last = Green|first = David B.|date = 16 December 2014|work = Haaretz|access-date = 1 August 2015}}</ref> In September, her father was ordered to report to the [[Gestapo]] office, where he was questioned and later sent to [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz]].<ref name=":1" /> Later that year, the [[Nazi Germany|Nazis]] were going to arrest the other [[History of the Jews in Norway|Jews]] in Oslo, however, Samuel-Cahn's family were moved by members of [[Norwegian resistance movement|the underground]], Ingebjørg Sletten-Fosstvedt and [[Sigrid Helliesen Lund]], to safety and later to a refugee camp in [[Sweden during World War II|neutral Sweden]].<ref name=":0" /> In order to cross [[Norway–Sweden border|the border]], Samuel-Cahn and the rest of her family had to hide in trucks used to transport potatoes.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.alemannia-judaica.de/images/Images%20318/Rabbi%20Isaak%20Samuel.pdf|title = Rabbi Isaak Samuel, הי"ד Rabbi of Norwegian Jewry|date = 2006|access-date = 1 August 2015|last1 = Samuel-Cahn|first1 = Ester|last2 = Samuel|first2 = Amos}}</ref> In [[Stockholm]], Samuel-Cahn's family found out that her father had been killed in Auschwitz.<ref name=":0" /> In 1946, Samuel-Cahn, her mother, and brothers moved to [[Mandatory Palestine]] (part of which later became Israel).<ref>{{Cite web|title = Holocaust/Heroism Day Begins Tonight|url = http://www.israelnationalnews.com/News/News.aspx/126020#.Vb1EBkCUzGc|website = Arutz Sheva|access-date = 2015-08-01|date = 30 April 2008|last = Fendel|first = Hillel}}</ref>

Samuel-Cahn received her Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]] in 1961.<ref name=":2" /> From 1993 to 1995, she was the president of the Israel Statistical Association.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://stat.haifa.ac.il/~isa/history.htm|title = History of the ISA|access-date = 1 August 2015|website = Israel Statistical Association|last = Weissman|first = Ishay|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070613224208/http://stat.haifa.ac.il/~isa/history.htm|archive-date = 13 June 2007|url-status = dead}}</ref>
In 1989, she was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-11-19.</ref> She was also a fellow of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] from 1989,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26861|title=Utenlandske medlemmer|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]]|language=no|access-date=2 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715102608/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=26861|archive-date=15 July 2007}}</ref> and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm|title=Honored Fellows|publisher=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|access-date=2017-11-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302125855/http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm|archive-date=2014-03-02|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2004, Samuel-Cahn won the [[List of Israel Prize recipients|Israel Prize]] for her work in statistics.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Center members have been awarded distinguished prizes|url = http://ratio.huji.ac.il/node/2491|website = The Hebrew University of Jerusalem - Center for the Study of Rationality|access-date = 2015-08-02}}</ref> In 2012, she spoke at a memorial ceremony in the [[Forest of the Martyrs|Martyrs' Forest]] in Jerusalem Hills, commemorating Norwegian Jews [[The Holocaust in Norway|murdered]] in [[the Holocaust]] and remembering those who helped hide and [[List of Norwegian Righteous Among the Nations|protect Jews in Norway]].<ref>{{Cite news|url = http://www.kkl.org.il/eng/about-kkl-jnf/green-israel-news/november-2012/norway-jews-memorial/|title = Martyrs' Forest Memorial Ceremony for Norwegian Jews Who Perished in the Holocaust|date = November 2012|work = Keren Kayemeth LeIsrael Jewish National Fund|access-date = 1 August 2015}}</ref>

She died in November 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last=Aderet |first=Ofer |date=2015-11-26 |title=הפרופסורית שפתרה את "בעיית המזכירה" |url=https://www.haaretz.co.il/.premium-1.2785463 |newspaper=[[Haaretz]] |access-date=2016-01-24 }}</ref>
